verifyNotes: node tools/verify-page.mjs --drafts /testing/unit-testing-fundamentals/ : FAIL only on the expected NEEDS_MARKUS placeholder (3 occurrences: byline, bio, footer legal name). words=2051, code=16, figures=1, h1=1, internalLinks=28, broken=[], mobileOverflowPx=0, consoleErrors=[], consoleWarnings=[]. Lighthouse 99/100/100/100. Screenshots read: all 8 desktop-light parts, all 12 mobile-dark parts (plus both folds), desktop-dark fold+part03+part04+part06, mobile-light fold+part04+part06+part09 (diagram and both `fails` panels in every theme/width combination checked).
justification: This clears the design bar comfortably. Rhythm is disciplined: short paragraphs, no wall of text, and a steady cadence of prose -> code -> output -> (diagram or exercise) all the way down; three exercises of genuinely different shapes (diagnose-a-failure, predict-then-verify, write-your-own-test) sit at natural pause points and every solution is correctly collapsed (`Show solution` triangle closed) in all four theme/width screenshot sets, including the nested exercise-inside-solution case in 'Find the bug'. Heading hierarchy is clean (only ##/### used, matches the on-this-page nav, no skipped levels). The single diagram (Figure 1, AAA test anatomy) follows the design system correctly: 360-wide portrait stack, annotations under each box rather than beside it, 12-14 unit text that stays crisp at 390px in both themes, a `d-box-accent` highlight on the Assert region that reads clearly against both light and dark backgrounds, and a caption that stands alone. Callouts (one pitfall, three exercises) are visually distinct from body text and from each other in dark mode, with no contrast problems. The two `fails`-flagged xUnit panels behave as the site's standard scroll-with-fade affordance intends rather than hard-clipping: the second one (summarize-after, a string-diff failure) is well-shaped for mobile — the test name is what scrolls off, but the load-bearing `Expected:`/`Actual:`/`pos 4` diff markers that the surrounding prose actually discusses all sit inside the visible ~40-column window in every screenshot. The first one (boundary-bug, a Theory-case failure) is very slightly worse: real xUnit renders the parameterized case name as one long line (`GradeCalculatorTests.LetterGrade_BoundaryScore_ReturnsExpectedGrade(average: 90, expected: 'A') [FAIL]`), which scrolls off past column ~40 on both mobile and desktop before the reader reaches `average: 90`; the `Expected: 'A'` / `Actual: 'B'` lines immediately below remain fully visible, so the pass/fail fact survives, but the specific input value the exercise and the following prose lean on ('the failing case name says it directly: average: 90, expected: 'A'') is not readable without scrolling on a phone. This is real captured tool output rather than something to reformat without becoming inaccurate, so it is a minor, isolated nit rather than the kind of repeated, central clipping that would cost more. Compared against two real top-ranking pages on this exact topic, the article is well ahead on the design/UX axis this review judges: Microsoft's own 'Unit testing best practices' page is static prose with code blocks and zero diagrams, zero interactivity, and no dark-theme or phone-specific design; xUnit's getting-started docs are plain reference documentation with no worked examples beyond isolated snippets and no exercises at all. This article's one hand-drawn, theme-correct diagram, three exercises with progressively-revealed solutions, and a real-vs-brittle-test worked comparison (with real, verified tool output, not paraphrased) is more illustrated and more interactive than either comparison source.

issues.location: `boundary-bug` output panel (Exercise 1 'Find the bug'), the failing-case line `GradeCalculatorTests.LetterGrade_BoundaryScore_ReturnsExpectedGrade(average: 90, expected: 'A') [FAIL]`; seen clipped in mobile-dark part06, mobile-light part06, and even desktop-light/desktop-dark part03-part04 where the box is much wider
issues.problem: The specific value the exercise hinges on ('average: 90') sits past the visible window of the output panel on every device width checked; only the class/method prefix is visible before the scroll fade. The `Expected: 'A'` / `Actual: 'B'` lines right below are fully visible, so the pass/fail fact is not lost, but a reader trying to solve the exercise from the output alone (rather than opening the solution) cannot see which of the three theory rows failed without manually scrolling the panel sideways.
issues.fixLooksLike: Not really fixable without altering real captured output (which the article correctly refuses to fake). Two options worth considering: (a) shorten `LetterGrade_BoundaryScore_ReturnsExpectedGrade` in this one exercise's test method to something a few characters shorter so `average: 90` lands inside the visible window, or (b) accept as-is since Expected/Actual still carries the pass/fail signal and the solution spells out the reasoning; not blocking.
